issues.description: The gloss for the target word 'headache' — 'when your head feels sick' — is inaccurate and teaches a wrong collocation. Native speakers do not say a head 'feels sick'; a headache is a pain in the head. A learner could wrongly conclude that 'sick' can describe a hurting body part (e.g. 'my head is sick').
issues.suggested_fix: Change the gloss to 'a pain in your head' (or 'when your head hurts'). Both use A2-level words and are accurate.

issues.description: The theme in the spec is 'feeling sick and visiting the pharmacy', but the dialogue only covers feeling sick and advice to see a doctor; the pharmacy never appears. Understandable given the 10-15 second micro-dialogue limit, but the theme is only half delivered.
issues.suggested_fix: Either adjust the theme to 'feeling sick and getting advice', or change line s1l3 to mention the pharmacy, e.g. 'You should go to the pharmacy. You shouldn't work today.'

qa_report.summary: A clean, level-appropriate micro-dialogue: all three lines are grammatically correct and natural, 'should/shouldn't' for advice is modelled twice and explained correctly, and every word is at or below A2 apart from the intended target 'headache'. One real problem: the English gloss for 'headache' ('when your head feels sick') is inaccurate and models a collocation native speakers do not use — it should read 'a pain in your head' or 'when your head hurts'. Minor note: the spec's theme mentions visiting the pharmacy, which never occurs in the clip. Fix the gloss and this is ready to record.
